atomic_claim_evaluations.heading: 5. Failure modes and limitations
atomic_claim_evaluations.exact_claim: If the initial dominant projection is exactly zero, exact multiplication cannot create it and the iteration may converge to a different represented eigendirection.

lesson_evidence.heading: 5. Failure modes and limitations
lesson_evidence.exact_excerpt: In exact arithmetic, if $c_1=0$, the dominant component is never created by multiplication, so the iteration may converge to the largest-magnitude eigenvector present in the initial vector instead.

atomic_claim_evaluations.rationale: Matches RC-012.

atomic_claim_evaluations.heading: 5. Failure modes and limitations
atomic_claim_evaluations.exact_claim: If $Ax_k=0$, the current vector lies in the nullspace and there is no next normalized direction.

lesson_evidence.heading: 5. Failure modes and limitations
lesson_evidence.exact_excerpt: The iteration can also break down when $Ax_k=0$. This occurs if the current vector is in the nullspace. It is not merely a normalization inconvenience: the algorithm has no next direction.

atomic_claim_evaluations.rationale: Entailed by the non-zero denominator and breakdown requirements.

atomic_claim_evaluations.heading: 5. Failure modes and limitations
